title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: A science fiction masterpiece set on the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the most valuable substance in the universe. A young nobleman navigates political intrigue, religion, and ecology in a saga that redefined the genre.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: A mathematician discovers psychohistory — a science that can predict the future of civilization. He sets in motion a plan to reduce 30,000 years of barbarism to a single millennium. A landmark of science fiction.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: The novel that defined cyberpunk. A washed-up computer hacker is hired for one last job — a caper with consequences that ripple through cyberspace and reality alike.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: An astronaut becomes stranded alone on Mars after his crew evacuates. Using his botany and engineering skills, he must survive and signal Earth. A gripping tale of ingenuity and humor.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
description: In a future war against an alien race, humanity trains child geniuses in battle school. Ender Wiggin may be the military genius Earth needs — but at what cost to his humanity?

title: Recursion
author: Blake Crouch
description: A neuroscientist's research into memory unlocks the ability to travel back in time and relive pivotal moments. What begins as a gift quickly unravels into an existential nightmare.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Told through the eyes of young Scout Finch in Alabama during the 1930s, this Pulitzer Prize-winning novel explores racial injustice and moral growth through the trial of a Black man wrongly accused.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: Set in the roaring 1920s, this story of Jay Gatsby's obsessive love for Daisy Buchanan is a searing critique of the American Dream and the hollowness of wealth and social status.

author: George Orwell
description: In a totalitarian future England, Winston Smith works for the Ministry of Truth rewriting history. His secret rebellion against Big Brother forms one of literature's most chilling dystopias.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young shepherd's journey from Spain to Egypt in search of treasure becomes a philosophical adventure about listening to your heart and following your dreams. A global phenomenon.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: The multi-generational story of the Buendía family in the fictional town of Macondo blends magical realism with themes of solitude, love, and the cyclical nature of history.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: A society engineered for happiness at the cost of freedom. Bernard Marx questions his world of conditioning and consumption in this prescient vision of a future too close for comfort.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
description: Journalist Mikael Blomkvist and hacker Lisbeth Salander investigate a decades-old disappearance connected to a powerful Swedish industrial dynasty. A gripping Scandinavian noir.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: On the morning of their fifth anniversary, Amy Dunne goes missing. Her husband Nick becomes the prime suspect. Told in alternating voices, this psychological thriller upends every expectation.

title: In the Woods
author: Tana French
description: A Dublin detective investigating a child's murder discovers a haunting link to a childhood trauma he cannot remember. A richly atmospheric crime debut from a master of psychological suspense.

title: The Name of the Rose
author: Umberto Eco
description: A medieval monk and his novice investigate a series of suspicious deaths in a remote Italian abbey. Equal parts historical mystery, philosophical treatise, and literary labyrinth.

title: Big Little Lies
author: Liane Moriarty
description: Three women's lives become entangled in a web of secrets, marriages, and parenting politics in a wealthy Australian school community — until a fatal trivia night reveals the truth.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
description: Four septuagenarian residents of a retirement village meet weekly to solve cold cases — until a real murder lands on their doorstep. Witty, warm, and wickedly clever.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A sweeping history of the human species from the first Homo sapiens to the present day, exploring how biology and history have defined us and enhanced our understanding of what it means to be human.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
description: A memoir of a woman who grew up in a survivalist family in rural Idaho, never attending school, and who through sheer tenacity educated herself all the way to a Cambridge PhD.

title: The Body: A Guide for Occupants
author: Bill Bryson
description: A witty and enlightening tour of the human body, covering everything from the microbiome to the brain to why we sleep, told with Bryson's trademark curiosity and humor.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman explores the two systems that drive the way we think: fast, intuitive System 1 and slow, deliberate System 2. Groundbreaking insights into human decision-making.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
description: The story of HeLa cells — the first immortal human cells ever grown in a laboratory — and the Black woman whose cancer cells were taken without her knowledge, fueling decades of medical research.

title: Quiet: The Power of Introverts
author: Susan Cain
description: An exploration of the power of introverts in a world that won't stop talking. Cain argues that modern Western culture misunderstands and undervalues the gifts of introverted people.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
description: The exclusive biography of Apple's visionary co-founder, based on over forty interviews with Jobs and hundreds more with family, friends, rivals, and colleagues. A portrait of creativity and tyranny.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: Anne Frank's diary, written while hiding from the Nazis in Amsterdam during World War II, is one of history's most powerful accounts of the Holocaust and a testament to the human spirit.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: In her memoir, the former First Lady charts her journey from the South Side of Chicago to the White House — a story of race, identity, family, and the relentless pursuit of excellence.

title: Long Walk to Freedom
author: Nelson Mandela
description: Nelson Mandela's autobiography chronicles the anti-apartheid movement, his 27 years in prison, and his triumphant emergence to lead South Africa as its first democratically elected president.

title: The Wright Brothers
author: David McCullough
description: Pulitzer Prize winner David McCullough tells the dramatic story of the Wright brothers, two self-taught bicycle mechanics who changed the world by achieving the first powered airplane flights.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson
description: Based on thousands of pages from da Vinci's notebooks, Isaacson weaves a narrative that connects his art to his science, and shows how his genius was driven by curiosity, experimentation, and imagination.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship. Uncle Bob's guide to writing code that is readable, maintainable, and elegant — with case studies, exercises, and hard-won wisdom.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
description: From journeyman to master: timeless lessons in software engineering that remain as relevant today as when first published. Covers career-shaping topics from DRY principles to debugging strategies.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: The definitive guide to building reliable, scalable, and maintainable data systems. Covers databases, distributed systems, stream processing, and the trade-offs between competing architectures.

title: The Phoenix Project
author: Gene Kim
description: A novel about IT, DevOps, and helping your business win. Bill faces a catastrophic IT failure and must transform the organization in 90 days — learning the principles that become DevOps.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
author: Betsy Beyer & others (Google)
description: How Google runs production systems at scale. The foundational text of SRE covers error budgets, SLOs, toil reduction, on-call practices, and building a culture of reliability.

title: Kubernetes in Action
author: Marko Lukša
description: A comprehensive guide to deploying and managing containerized applications in Kubernetes. Covers pods, services, deployments, StatefulSets, networking, and cluster security.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: A practical guide to building good habits and breaking bad ones, grounded in science. Clear's four-law framework — make it obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying — is transformative.

title: The Power of Now
author: Eckhart Tolle
description: A guide to spiritual enlightenment that teaches readers to recognize the self-sabotaging patterns of the mind and live fully in the present moment. A global bestseller.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor E. Frankl
description: A Holocaust survivor and psychiatrist describes his experiences in Auschwitz and uses them to illustrate his theory of logotherapy — that meaning, not pleasure, is the primary motivational force.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
description: A principle-centered approach to personal and professional effectiveness. Covey's seven habits framework has become a touchstone for leadership and personal development worldwide.

title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
author: Carol S. Dweck
description: Stanford psychologist Carol Dweck reveals how our beliefs about our own abilities profoundly impact all areas of our lives, and how a growth mindset leads to success.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
description: Rules for focused success in a distracted world. Newport argues that the ability to perform deep work — cognitively demanding tasks without distraction — is a superpower in today's economy.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning exploration of why some civilizations conquered others. Diamond argues that geography, not race or intelligence, explains the differential fates of peoples.

title: The Silk Roads: A New History
author: Peter Frankopan
description: A radical retelling of world history from the perspective of the routes connecting East and West. Shows how the flow of goods, people, and ideas shaped civilizations from antiquity to the present.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
description: Cambridge classicist Mary Beard explores how Rome grew from a cluster of huts on the Tiber to a global empire, challenging myths and bringing the ancient world to vivid life.

title: The Guns of August
author: Barbara Tuchman
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning account of the first month of World War I, revealing how a combination of rigid military planning and diplomatic failures led the world into catastrophic war.

title: The Storm Before the Storm
author: Mike Duncan
description: The forgotten history of the Roman Republic's final decades before Julius Caesar — a cautionary tale about how democracy can unravel through populism, political violence, and institutional decay.

title: Alexander Hamilton
author: Ron Chernow
description: The definitive biography of America's most misunderstood Founding Father. Hamilton's rags-to-riches story, his extraordinary achievements, and his fatal rivalry with Aaron Burr.
